title: Clear music out of pain, and the Birdland engagement
summary: The pristine music was written out of pain; he took the band to Birdland for two weeks opposite Basie.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: To refer to that past matter for just a moment, this was done in the midst of the narcotics days?
Yeah.
It was enormously clear music and it's enormously clear George Handy and terribly professional and all those things; how does that square with--
It's astonishing; it was written out of a lot of pain.
You were able to overcome the pain to the point of being that clear and that pristeen?
I think when you get that involved with work, pain doesn't exist.
Naive question, if it
I wouldn't know how to answer that.
Strike that, transcriber.
Take it out.
It has no hint of any other problem, it doesn't even sound hurried or like you needed the two thousand dollars to pay the rent or whatever.
My work didn't seem to be any different before or during.
There are tapes of that book being played later on as the George Handy orchestra in Birdland.
Say that again, Bill?
You took that book to Birdland.
That was the band I took to Birdland; right.
Was that just for a moment, or did you campaign that band around town or around the country?
No, that was the only date we played.
How long were you there?
Two weeks.
What kind of reaction was that?
It was well received. It was very well received. We were there opposite Basie, which was a groove. He had a great band there.
What did the Basie people think of the George Handy band?
I think they liked it, we never got into deep discussion.
Did they stand around the band?
They listened; right.
And you all sat around
Yes, we did.
What else was happening in those days?
